description.value:
Selecting this pursuit grants access to a set of discoveries drawn from your ongoing medical research. Each time you gain a new discovery, you may pick from the list below as well, presented here alphabetically.

Advanced Remote Healer (11th level required). Your Remote Healer's range extends to 60 feet.

Experimental Treatments. Your remedies are notoriously unpredictable. Right after using a maneuver that restores hit points or grants temporary hit points to a creature, you can choose to roll a d20 on the following table of side effects. Whatever results lasts until the creature finishes a long rest or you trigger this feature on it again.

  • 1 — Turns out the creature is allergic to this exact treatment: every one of its ability scores drops by 1.
  • 2 — Uncontrollable sneezing sets in; any attack roll that comes up as a natural 19 counts as a miss thanks to an ill-timed sneeze.
  • 3 — The creature's legs swell painfully, giving it 1 slowed level.
  • 4 — The creature's size shifts one category larger or smaller.
  • 5 — The joints harden into a wood-like material, granting a +2 bonus to AC.
  • 6 — The body begins manufacturing potent stomach acid. As an action, the creature can spew it in a 15-foot cone; the save DC equals 8 plus its proficiency bonus plus its Constitution modifier, dealing 2d6 acid damage (half on a success). That damage rises to 3d6 at 5th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 17th level.
  • 7 — The creature loses its voice and develops uncontrollable flatulence, giving it disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks that depend on smell.
  • 8 — The eyes flare bright red, granting darkvision — or, if the creature already had darkvision, giving it a mild headache instead.
  • 9 — Hearing sharpens dramatically, granting advantage on Perception checks based on sound, but everything now sounds painfully loud, giving the creature vulnerability to sonic damage.
  • 10 — Cognitive function dulls: Intelligence drops by 4.
  • 11 — The skin turns deep purple — or, if it was already purple, it instead turns bright pink.
  • 12 — The skin erupts in sickly green pustules; any creature that hits it with a melee attack takes 1d4 poison damage in return.
  • 13 — Internal pressure builds dangerously beneath the skin. Whenever the creature takes damage, it must succeed on a concentration check or take kinetic damage equal to half its maximum hit points, with other creatures within 10 feet taking a quarter of that damage; once this rupture happens, the resulting skin is notably softer.
  • 14 — Thick body hair sprouts everywhere, including the face, until the creature looks like a wookiee — or, if it's already a wookiee, the opposite happens and all its hair falls out.
  • 15 — Body temperature swings wildly, granting resistance to both cold and fire damage.
  • 16 — Hunger becomes ravenous; for every hour that passes without the creature eating, it gains a level of exhaustion.
  • 17 — The creature becomes convinced it is destined for greatness — a belief with no mechanical effect.
  • 18 — Rest no longer comes easily: hit points recovered from spending Hit Dice are halved.
  • 19 — Movement speed increases by 15 feet, and opportunity attacks against the creature are made with disadvantage.
  • 20 — The creature gains 10d10 hit points and an inexplicable sense of contentment.

You can trigger this feature twice, gaining one more use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level, and you regain all spent uses on finishing a short or long rest.

From the Brink (7th level required). When your Critical Analysis target would drop to 0 hit points, you can spend your reaction and end your Critical Analysis to leave them at 1 hit point instead. A creature that benefits this way needs a long rest before it can be saved by this feature again.

Health Advisor. When your Critical Analysis target starts its turn, you may use your reaction to grant it temporary hit points equal to one-quarter your scholar level plus your proficiency bonus; these last until the start of that creature's next turn.

Patient Protector (5th level required). Any creature within 5 feet of your Critical Analysis target can be treated as though it, too, were a target of your Critical Analysis.

Surgical Precision (5th level required). Hitting your Critical Analysis target with a weapon attack deals extra damage equal to your Dexterity modifier.

Tend the Wounded. When you or any friendly creature within your reach recovers hit points by spending Hit Dice at the end of a short rest, that creature regains an extra 1d4 hit points. This bonus die upgrades as you level up: 1d6 at 5th level, 1d8 at 9th, 1d10 at 13th, and 1d12 at 17th.
